title: EPIQ
text: EPIQ carries WOAH’s epidemic intelligence and much more: disease situation reports, ad-hoc analyses and the integration of surveillance data. It combines official data reported by Members with non-official sources scouted by WOAH, such as online media and data sources identified for rapid risk assessment.

title: EPIQ
text: EPIQ carries WOAH’s epidemic intelligence and much more: disease situation reports, ad-hoc analyses and the integration of surveillance data. It combines official data reported by Members with non-official sources scouted by WOAH, such as online media and data sources identified for rapid risk assessment.

title: EPIQ
text:
Where we are going


Integrated intelligence
Official and non-official data, unified across WOAH.


Anticipatory risk intelligence
From event detection to trends, foresight and modelling.


Decision support, at scale
Feeding WOAH risk assessments, powered by automation and AI.



Highlights of the year

Data scouting: mapping and assessment of data sources for rapid risk assessment, globally and with a regional focus.
Situation reports: streamlined production, soon published on a public Git page (this site).
Horizon scanning: online media data integrated for early detection of emerging threats.

title: About DIAD
text:
DIAD turns WOAH data into evidence and advice. It is organised in three business teams and one transversal team:

The Observatory monitors the implementation of WOAH standards by Members.
EPIQ, the EPIdemiology & Quantitative intelligence group, runs epidemic intelligence and risk analytics.
Animal Health Econometrics studies the economics of animal health.
The Data Science Lab provides data products, pipelines, automation and AI to all of WOAH.

title: About DIAD
section: DIAD in the WOAH data strategy
text:
DIAD in the WOAH data strategy
DIAD leads the data side of the WOAH data strategy, from collection to external sharing.







Step
Where we are going




Collect
Increase the quality and coverage of officially reported data. Make automated online media monitoring and data scouting part of routine rapid risk assessment.


Curate
Complete the glossary, with DOIs.


Analyse
Publish situation reports openly. Leverage our network of collaborators to create value from WOAH data.


Share internally
Bring all technical datasets onto Fabric, with ownership kept by departments.


Share externally
Master datasets available through the API. MCP project for AI access.



These objectives contribute to three outcomes of WOAH’s 8th Strategic Plan: standards adaptable to all Members; decision-making to tackle global challenges; and leadership in animal health data.

title: The Observatory
text:
The Observatory monitors the uptake of WOAH international standards by Members and formulates recommendations to improve them and their implementation. Its data come from Members through the official channel, mainly through ad-hoc Thematic Studies, and increasingly from complementary sources such as national legislation.

The Observatory works at capacity and is moving towards sharper, more targeted and more robust output.


Routine reporting
Regular, reproducible outputs replacing one-off production, planned within the next 6 months.


Prescriptive analysis
From describing implementation gaps to recommending actions Members and WOAH can take.


Diversified data sources
New sources beyond thematic studies, including AI-supported analysis of the FAOLEX legislation database.

title: Data Science Lab
text: The DS Lab is DIAD’s transversal team. It builds the data foundations that the three business teams, and other WOAH departments, rely on: data products on Microsoft Fabric, data management and analytics pipelines, process automation and ad-hoc analyses. It also spearheads AI adoption across the Organisation.

title: Data Science Lab
text: The DS Lab is DIAD’s transversal team. It builds the data foundations that the three business teams, and other WOAH departments, rely on: data products on Microsoft Fabric, data management and analytics pipelines, process automation and ad-hoc analyses. title: Data Science Lab
text:
What we build


Master datasets
Countries, diseases and disease status (glossary forthcoming): one reference version for all of WOAH, citable through DOIs.


APIs for programs
Master datasets made available to programs through an API, with no human in the loop.


Data for AI (MCP)
A project to make WOAH data directly queryable by AI assistants through the Model Context Protocol.


AI adoption
Tools such as a translation app and a standards query app, and an MSc-AI internship programme scaling AI into daily use.


One platform
Microsoft Fabric Lakehouses as the single storage platform, with ownership kept by technical departments.
